notes: Sources: CAREER lists with 10 rows come from the CAREER TOP 10 tables (pdf p432-433, printed rank numbers, blank rank = tie); the rest come from the INDIVIDUAL RECORDS pages (pdf p439-446: 'Most X - Career/Season/Game', top 5, no rank numbers). pdf page numbers equal the printed page numbers in this guide ('2026 MEDIA GUIDE 440' on pdf p440). Every digit was read from 200-300 dpi crops of the page pictures; the first five rows of each TOP 10 career table were also checked by script against the INDIVIDUAL RECORDS top 5 and match.

Season and game lists use the INDIVIDUAL RECORDS pages (top 5 and ties); the guide's TOP 10 SEASONS (p435) and TOP 10 GAME PERFORMANCES (p437) tables show the same top rows (read and compared by eye: rushing yards, passing yards, receptions, receiving yards, interceptions all agree) but were not transcribed beyond rank 5 on purpose.

through_season is 2025: the lists include 2025 entries (Myles Garrett 23 sacks in 2025, Myles Garrett 5 sacks on 10/26/2025, Devin Bush 2025 in the TD-on-interception line, a Jan. 4, 2026 game at Cincinnati on the Longest Plays page p438); the guide is the 2026 edition dated 2026-07-21.

Regular season only: the guide does not title these pages 'regular season', but its all-time game lists mark playoff games '(playoffs)' and Bernie Kosar's 489-yard playoff game (1/3/1987 vs. New York Jets, listed on p474) is absent from the passing-yards lists, so postseason games are not in these lists. Records page 'Postseason' section: none found.

AAFC (1946-49) years are not in these lists: every printed career span starts in 1950 or later (Otto Graham 1950-55, Lou Groza 1950-59, Tommy James 1950-55), and p433 carries the footnote '*Does not include AAFC statistics' (attached to Dante Lavelli 1950-56* in the average-per-reception table). So the 1946-49 Browns seasons contribute nothing to any list here.

The guide prints no rank numbers on the INDIVIDUAL RECORDS pages: rank here = printed order, ties share the lower rank and carry tie=true. On the CAREER TOP 10 pages the rank numbers are printed (a blank rank = tie with the row above) and the same rule gives the same ranks.

Season rushing TDs: the printed line '17 Jim Brown (1958, 1965)' is one line for two seasons; it is split into two rows (1958, 1965), both with raw = the printed line. The TOP 10 SEASONS rushing table (p435) shows 17 TDs for both 1958 and 1965, which agrees.

Aggregate lines: four game lists have no per-game list because the guide prints 'N times; most recently: <player> (<date>)' - game pass_td (5, six times, Baker Mayfield 10/25/2020), game rec_td (3, 11 times, Jordan Cameron 9/22/2013), game int (3, 11 times, Anthony Henry 11/18/2001) and the fourth line of game rec (11 receptions, seven times, Jerry Jeudy 12/15/2024). Each is entered as ONE row flagged tie=true with complete_to=1 (or the 4 printed lines for rec); it is a real printed game but NOT the whole set of tied holders.

Game receptions: the INDIVIDUAL RECORDS line says '11 ... Seven times' while the p437 TOP 10 GAME PERFORMANCES table prints eight games with 11 receptions (Speedie, Slaughter, Johnson, Winslow x3, Cooper, Jeudy); the count is a guide inconsistency, not used.

Sacks: footnote '*Sacks became an official stat in 1982, any figure prior is unofficial.' Rows marked * in the guide are kept with the * in raw: career Clay Matthews (1978-93)*, Jerry Sherk (1970-81)*, Walter Johnson (1965-76)*; season Bill Glass 1965*, Jack Gregory 1970*; game Jerry Sherk 1976*, Mack Mitchell 1977*. Clay Matthews' career total spans 1978-93, so part of it is unofficial.

Game rec_yds: the printed text for Josh Gordon's 261-yard game has a typo ('vs, Jacksonville Jaguars' with a comma); written as 'vs. Jacksonville Jaguars'. Typographic oddities only, no digits changed.

While reading the p437 TOP 10 GAME PERFORMANCES passing table I saw that the guide prints '1/10/1986' for Bernie Kosar's 401-yard game vs. Miami (the same game is 11/10/1986 on p333, p449 and p474): a guide typo, relevant only if someone transcribes that table beyond rank 5; no row in the JSON uses it.
Names are as printed (Jim Brown, Leroy Kelly, Earnest Byner, Michael Dean Perry ...); the IA OCR text shows 'J im' for 'Jim', the page pictures show 'Jim'.
